::: {#exm-expectation-die}
#### Expectation of a fair die roll

Let $Y$ be the result of a fair die roll,
so the [range](random-variables.qmd#def-range) is $\rangef{Y} =\set{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}$ and $\P(Y=y) = 1/6$ for each $y$ in the range.
Every value has the same weight,
so the [expectation](#def-expectation) is the ordinary [mean](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-vectors.html#def-mean) of $1, \ldots, 6$:

$$
\ba
\E{Y}
&= \sum_{y \in \set{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}} y \cd \P(Y=y)
&& \text{(definition of expectation for discrete r.v.)}\\
&= \paren{1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6} \cd \frac{1}{6}
&& \text{(every weight is } 1/6 \text{)}\\
&= \frac{21}{6}
&& \text{(add)}\\
&= 3.5
&& \text{(divide)}
\ea
$$

Now load the die so that the result $6$ has [probability](probability-basics.qmd#def-probability) $1/2$,
and each of $1, \ldots, 5$ has probability $1/10$.
The weights still add to $1$, and the expectation moves toward $6$:

$$
\ba
\E{Y}
&= \paren{1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5} \cd \frac{1}{10} + 6 \cd \frac{1}{2}
&& \text{(weights } 1/10 \text{ and } 1/2 \text{)}\\
&= 1.5 + 3
&& \text{(multiply)}\\
&= 4.5
&& \text{(add)}
\ea
$$

:::
